title: MAP for Broadband Funding Act
official_title: An Act to modernize and improve the Broadband Funding Map in order to promote the most efficient use of Federal funds for broadband deployment, and for other purposes.
likelihoodReason: Sponsored by Sen. Deb Fischer (R-NE) with bipartisan support (cosponsored by Sen. Catherine Cortez Masto, D-NV). A narrow, low-cost broadband-mapping measure — an FCC notice of inquiry plus a GAO study with no direct appropriations — the kind of technical oversight bill that commonly clears the House.
summary: Directs the FCC, working with the NTIA, to keep the federal Broadband Funding Map up to date and to seek public input on improving it, and orders a GAO study of how well agencies maintain the map. The map tracks where federal broadband-deployment dollars go to prevent paying twice to wire the same area.
brief: Requires the FCC to modernize and seek public comment on the Broadband Funding Map and orders a GAO study of how federal agencies maintain it.

top_lines.headline: What the Broadband Funding Map Does
subs: Federal map showing the location of each federally funded broadband project
Meant to prevent redundant overbuilding with federal funds

top_lines.headline: FCC Map Modernization
subs: FCC must collect agency data for the map on a timely basis
Must open a notice of inquiry within 270 days on the map's functionality
Must complete the inquiry within 120 days of starting it

top_lines.headline: GAO Study
subs: GAO must report within 180 days on agency compliance and map management
Reviews whether the FCC has authority to collect the needed data

items.main: Names the Act the “Modernization, Accountability, and Planning for Broadband Funding Act” (the “MAP for Broadband Funding Act”).
items.detail: Short-title section — citation name only; no substantive effect.

items.main: Defines key terms used throughout the Act: appropriate congressional committees, Broadband Funding Map, broadband infrastructure, Commission, and NTIA.
items.detail: Definitions apply throughout; "Broadband Funding Map" and "broadband infrastructure" take the meanings given in section 60105(a) of the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (47 U.S.C. 1704(a)); "Commission" means the FCC.

items.main: Directs the FCC, in coordination with the NTIA, to collect data for the Broadband Funding Map on a reasonable and timely basis to promote the most efficient use of federal funds for broadband deployment and prevent inefficient use or fragmentation of federal funding for broadband infrastructure.
items.detail: Within 270 days the FCC must open a notice of inquiry on the map's functionality and transparency, evaluating the adequacy and usability of submitted data, the timeliness of agency updates, whether the scope of reported data should expand, whether third-party mapping data should be incorporated to improve the map's functionality and transparency, and how the map could be integrated with existing FCC mapping tools. Before initiating the inquiry, any Commissioner may request a vote at the Commission level, and if one is requested the inquiry may not proceed unless a majority of Commissioners vote to approve it. The inquiry must be completed within 120 days of its initiation.

items.main: Requires the Government Accountability Office to study and report within 180 days on the roles, responsibilities, and progress of federal agencies in maintaining the Broadband Funding Map.
items.detail: The study must review each agency's data-submission compliance, the FCC's management of the map and interagency collaboration, whether the FCC has sufficient authority to collect the necessary data, the NTIA's broadband data-collection efforts under existing law, coordination among agencies that fund broadband (including USDA, HHS, Treasury, HUD, and the Institute of Museum and Library Services), how broader use of the map could improve taxpayer savings, and the feasibility and potential benefits of incorporating third-party mapping data into the map.

underreported.summary: The GAO study must assess whether the FCC has sufficient authority to collect the necessary data from federal agencies to populate the map.
underreported.why_unreported: This flags a potential authority gap in the existing mapping regime, distinct from the bill's map-modernization headline.

underreported.summary: The FCC's data collection is tied to preventing "redundant overbuilding of broadband infrastructure with Federal funding."
underreported.why_unreported: The operative aim is avoiding duplicate federal spending on the same areas, beyond simply updating a map.

gaps: The bill orders an FCC inquiry and a GAO study but does not require the FCC to act on the findings or change the map.
The bill aims to prevent redundant overbuilding but creates no enforcement mechanism to stop duplicative funding.
The bill directs review of FCC data-collection authority but does not itself grant the FCC new authority to compel agency data.
The bill lists agencies whose coordination GAO must review but does not require those agencies to submit data on a fixed schedule.

featured_quotes.name: Mrs. Fischer
featured_quotes.text: I rise today to discuss an issue that is near and dear to the State of Nebraska and to rural America, and that is the issue of closing the digital divide for unserved and underserved communities. My husband Bruce and I raised our family on a cattle ranch near Valentine, NE, so I know what it means to  live in a community where reliable internet is a luxury--it is not a given--and I know the opportunities rural America is missing as a result, from education and telehealth to entrepreneurship and precision agriculture.

added: FCC notice of inquiry on the Broadband Funding Map within 270 days (Sec 3)
GAO study and report on agency map compliance within 180 days (Sec 4)
New "Request for vote" provision: any Commissioner may request a Commission vote before the notice of inquiry, which may not proceed unless a majority of Commissioners approve it
New inquiry consideration (E): whether third-party mapping data should be incorporated to improve the Broadband Funding Map's functionality and transparency
New GAO study review item (7): the feasibility and potential benefits of incorporating third-party mapping data into the Broadband Funding Map
modified: Sec. 3(a) policy goal reworded from preventing "redundant overbuilding of broadband infrastructure" to preventing "inefficient use or fragmentation of Federal funding for broadband infrastructure"
